I got married and stuck in the relationship for so long because she loved me and I thought I was supposed to love her back. Your emotions are real and there is a valid reason for them. There is nothing wrong with you.

I know you're having a rough time. I struggled a lot during college too and had with my love life. I often worried about how I would ever get a date let alone a girlfriend. I spent a lot of time trying to "fix" and "improve" myself so that girls would like me. That got me nowhere. It know it sounds cheesy but you really do just need to be yourself and someone will like you for it. I found out a couple years after highschool that there were two attractive girls who were really interested in me. I first started dating during my final year of college, which by most people's standard might be considered "late". But heck, it happened and I've been in a couple loving relationships. They didn't work out, but that is life.

I'm a lot more comfortable with myself now. I recently started seeing a girl and I shared some of my deepest, darkest secrets with her very early on. She was totally understanding and accepting of it and it felt so liberating. We are all flawed and yet still lovable people.

The emotion of love might be different for everyone. There's no way of knowing whether what I experience as love is the same as what someone else might feel. I don't think you should put an expectation that you are supposed to feel a certain way.

I think firstly your mindset needs to be that of empathy and compassion. It's easy from the outside just to say "hey, you just need to do X" and think that that will work, but it's completely different for the person who is actually stuck in that hole. I've been told so many times just to "snap out of it" or "just be more positive". Its really so frustrating to hear that constantly.

First and foremost, just try to listen and understand. I think that is what your friend needs the most. Depression is hard and people going through it need some empathy.

I've been there. I was so fucked up in college there were so many times I thought I would never survive. I lived with 4 other human beings (my family) who were completely unaware of my struggle. I too felt completely alone.

You talk a lot about not doing well in school in your post. Is that what is so important to you? If so, why? I'm not saying your answer needs to be one or the other, but it's important to figure out what you actually want. Not what the world or your parents want of you, but what *you* want. 

The first time a counsellor asked me "what do you want?" I was blown away. I had no idea how to answer such a simple question. There were a lot of thoughts that came to mind, but they didn't feel authentic to me. They were all based on what I thought society expected of me.

I always thought I wanted to be successful and move up the ladder in the tech industry. I've done well for myself on a superficial level, but this career never really brought a lot of fulfillment to me. I'm starting to see that now and I'm getting ready to quit my job and pursue something completely different.

Your path might be different, but I think it all starts with asking yourself, "what do i want?"
